title: The Hill Above the Meuse in Thread: Krasnoyarsk, Rockville, and the Tree the Needle Walked
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Krasnoyarsk, and Nineteen Years of Other People's Ink

stops.name: Krasnoyarsk, the Surikov college
stops.date_confidence: placeholder year, month and day defaulted; katrinvates.com/art-cv attests the school and gives no dates whatever, and no source located gives her birth date or birthplace
stops.campa: On the Yenisei, in a city built where the river cuts the taiga, she is taught to draw at the art college that carries Surikov's name. The CV she will keep in English decades later gives the school and gives no years, so how long she stays or what she carries out of it cannot be said. What is certain is the order of the training. She learns to draw before she learns anything else, and the thread waits twenty years. Nothing in the record names a birth, a birthplace, or a family. The account of her life begins here, at a drawing board, already partway through.
suggested_refs: Krasnoyarsk Surikov Art College, named for the painter of the Boyarina Morozova

stops.name: Krasnoyarsk, the prepress bench
stops.date_confidence: placeholder year; katrinvates.com/about attests approximately nineteen years of graphic and prepress work and gives neither a start nor an end, and does not say in which country they were worked
stops.campa: Nineteen years, by her own count, at other people's images: a graphic and prepress designer preparing files for presses that will print them once and throw the plates away. She sets colour that somebody else has chosen, in registrations that must be exact and are never signed. It is a discipline of tolerances measured in fractions of a millimetre, and it is the entire apprenticeship the record gives her. No source names the studios, the clients, or the country in which the nineteen years are worked.
suggested_refs: Prepress colour separation as an unsigned craft, the trade she leaves for embroidery

stops.name: Krasnoyarsk, the departure no source records
stops.date_confidence: undocumented; no source located in this research gives a date, a season, or a reason for the emigration from Russia to the United States, and the year here is a placeholder marking a blank, not an estimate
stops.campa: Somewhere in these years she leaves Russia for the United States, and no source located gives the date, the port, the reason, or the season. The crossing is recorded as a blank, with no bridge built over it. What enters at one end is a prepress designer in Siberia; what comes out at the other is a woman in a Maryland suburb with a needle she has not yet picked up. Between them the record holds nothing at all. The journey has a hole in it here, and the hole is left open.
suggested_refs: The undocumented emigration, stated as a gap per house style
sources: no source located covering birth, birthplace, or emigration

stops.name: Rockville, Maryland, the needle taken up
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on katrinvates.com/about, month and day unknown and defaulted; note the flat contradiction with the 2018 publication credit on her own CV, recorded at the London stop and not resolved here
stops.campa: In a town on the northern edge of Washington she begins to embroider, taught by nobody. The website will call it self-taught and give the year and no more. She works on linen, and she works without a hoop. The cloth is held in the hand and the tension is judged by feel, so the fabric is never told in advance what shape it has to take. She builds the picture in passes, the way a painter does, and the linen answers to her grip alone. Nineteen years of preparing other people's colour end here.
suggested_refs: Free-style surface embroidery worked without hoop or frame, the technique she teaches later

stops.name: London, the year that will not reconcile
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on katrinvates.com/art-cv and directly contradicted by katrinvates.com/about, which dates the first stitch to 2019; two self-published pages on one domain, neither acknowledging the other, and the contradiction is left standing
stops.campa: Be Creative Magazine prints her in the United Kingdom, and her own CV dates it to 2018. Her own about page dates the first stitch to 2019. The two pages sit on one website, neither acknowledging the other, and they are set here side by side without choosing between them. The credit may be for design work out of the nineteen years, or the start date may be rounded, or one of the two numbers may be a typing error nobody has caught in eight years. Nothing in the evidence favours any of the three, so the record is left contradicting itself.
suggested_refs: Be Creative Magazine (UK), 2018 and again 2022, the earliest credit on her CV

stops.name: Chicago, Colossal takes up the work
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV, month and day unknown and defaulted; the coordinate is the outlet's city of record and not a place she is attested to have visited
stops.campa: The art site Colossal runs her landscapes, and the year turns into a circuit. Le Temps De Broder prints her in Switzerland, World Open News in Italy, Design You Trust in Spain, Twisted Sifter back in the United States. She has been stitching for two years. The pictures travel faster than she does: fog on a hillside, autumn in crimson and pine and gold, worked in floss and photographed close enough that a viewer has to be told it is not paint. Nobody has yet commissioned anything from her.
suggested_refs: Colossal, Le Temps De Broder, World Open News, Design You Trust, Twisted Sifter, all 2021

stops.name: Melbourne, frankie carries her south
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV; coordinate is the magazine's city of record, not an attested visit
stops.campa: The Australian magazine frankie carries her below the equator in the same year, completing a circuit of five continents inside twelve months. The work travels as an image of itself, reproduced at magazine scale, where the stitch reads as brushwork and the deception is the point. She is still an amateur by her own account and will not call herself professional for another year. On the platforms the readers come first and the standing comes after; in a gallery the order runs the other way.
suggested_refs: frankie magazine (Australia), 2021

stops.name: Taipei, DPI and the second name
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV; coordinate is the magazine's city of record, not an attested visit
stops.campa: DPI prints her in Taiwan, and Be Creative in the United Kingdom runs her a second time. The name that travels is not the one on her passport: it is Katrin Vates, the working name under which the embroidery is signed and sold, kept in use here long after her legal name is known. She is one hand under two names, filed under Sinchinova and cited as Vates, in the manner of the two other journeys that already name her at a tree in Lorraine she has not at this point stitched.
suggested_refs: DPI magazine (Taiwan), 2022; Be Creative Magazine (UK), second appearance 2022

stops.name: Seoul, Stitch&Trip and the count of platforms
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV; coordinate is the outlet's city of record, not an attested visit
stops.campa: Stitch&Trip carries her in South Korea and Netolabo in Japan, a needleworker in a Maryland suburb reaching two countries whose own embroidery traditions are older than the village she is about to spend a winter depicting. The count is now eleven outlets across nine countries in four years. None of the eleven is a museum, a catalogue, or a scholarly notice, and none of the later ones will be either. Her reception exists on platforms and nowhere else, and no institution has yet written a line about her.
suggested_refs: Stitch&Trip (South Korea) and Netolabo (Japan), both 2022

stops.name: Rockville, the profession declared
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on katrinvates.com/about, which gives 2022 as the professional launch after several years of self-taught practice; an earlier research pass gave 2021 and the site carries no 2021 milestone of any kind
stops.campa: She launches the artistic career professionally, by her own website's account, three years after the first stitch. The work does not change; the standing does. An Etsy shop takes orders for kits and finished pieces. A YouTube channel shows the hand at work. The Instagram following climbs toward the six figures it will be holding four years later. Within months the first commission arrives, from a client who wants a hillside in Lorraine and knows exactly which one.
suggested_refs: Etsy shop KatVatesEmbroidery; YouTube channel @KatrinVatesArt
sources: Etsy KatVatesEmbroidery and YouTube @KatrinVatesArt, via linked profiles

stops.name: Rockville, the first commissioned work
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the blog post attests the commission and gives no start date, and the work is announced finished on 19 January 2023, so a late-2022 start is reconstruction from the in-progress post of 22 December
stops.campa: Somebody asks her to make a picture for him. It is the first time anyone has, and she will say so plainly on her own blog when the work is done. The client is named on that page as Dr. Doeg. The subject is a village on the Meuse and a tree above it, which means the commission arrives with its own reading list attached: a trial record of 1431, a rehabilitation inquiry of 1456, a beech, a spring, a tower, and three virgin martyrs the parchment does not agree about.
stops.quote: This picture is my first commissioned art.
stops.quote_source: Ekaterina Sinchinova, blog post 'Domremy. The story of the picture,' katrinvates.com/blog/blbrj44pjcc57mrf90eunqqwektyzb
suggested_refs: The commission of the Domremy panel, her first, per her own blog

stops.name: Rockville, linen and no hoop, twenty inches by thirty
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the physical description reaches this file through a WebFetch summary of the blog post rather than the raw page, so the dimensions and the stitch list are carried as unverified against primary text
stops.campa: Twenty by thirty on linen, held in the hand. Straight stitch, chain stitch, French knots, and stitches she invents as the picture demands them. What builds under the needle is a green hillside, a well beside a great tree, a small tower with a single window, and a sky worked pink into blue. The description is her own, reaching this record through a tool's summary rather than the raw page, so every number in it is carried as reconstruction. She reports enjoying the process.
stops.quote_source: Ekaterina Sinchinova, blog post 'Domremy. The story of the picture,' katrinvates.com/blog/blbrj44pjcc57mrf90eunqqwektyzb
suggested_refs: The panel itself, 20 by 30 inches on linen, worked without hoop or frame

stops.name: Rockville, the picture posted in progress
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, but the caption wording reaches this file through a fetch of search results rather than the Instagram page itself, so the phrasing is provisional; this post is distinct from the completion reel of 19 January 2023 and is not merged with it
stops.campa: Two days before Christmas she posts the work unfinished and names it. The caption reaches this record by way of a search index rather than the page itself, so the wording is carried as provisional, a caution that applies to a sentence typed in a Maryland suburb and read within the day on six continents. The title is not provisional. She has decided to call it Domremy, a name that will outlast the unfinished stitches in it, worked on the first commission anyone has ever given her.
stops.quote: The picture is called Domrémy, this is the town in France in the process
stops.quote_source: Ekaterina Sinchinova, Instagram @katrin.vates, post of 22 December 2022, retrieved via fetch of search results and not the page itself
suggested_refs: Instagram @katrin.vates, the in-progress post of 22 December 2022
sources: Instagram @katrin.vates, 22 December 2022, via DuckDuckGo results fetch

stops.name: Rockville, the reel of the nineteenth of January
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, caption fetched verbatim from instagram.com/reel/CnmoJnOB2Nq; an earlier research pass dated this post to December 2022 and described it as work in progress, and both are wrong
stops.campa: She finishes and says so, in Russian and then in English, with two hearts in the colours of a flag that is not hers and is at war. Eleven thousand people mark the post. The comments arrive in several languages. She promises detail photographs later. The picture is dated from this caption and not from the December one, this one having been read directly: the December post shows a picture being made, and this one announces a picture made. They are two posts and they are not merged.
stops.quote: Domrémy / Сегодня окончила картину, ура ) / 💙💛 / Today I finished the picture ^^ / Domrémy (the town in France) / Later 'll take a photos and show the picture in details
stops.quote_source: Ekaterina Sinchinova, Instagram @katrin.vates, reel CnmoJnOB2Nq, 19 January 2023, caption verbatim
suggested_refs: Instagram reel CnmoJnOB2Nq, the completion announcement, roughly 11,300 likes

stops.name: Rockville, the story of the picture written out
stops.date_confidence: the blog post is dated September with no year stated in the fetched summary; the year is inferred as 2023 from the January 2023 completion, and the month is carried as given
stops.campa: On her blog she sets down what the picture holds, and it is not a decorator's note. She gives the village, the birth of 1412, the trial under oath that is the reason anything at all is known, the visions from the age of thirteen, the archangels Michael and Gabriel, and then the three virgin martyr saints by name: Catherine, Barbara and Margaret. She gives the beech, the garlands left for the fairies, the Bourlemont family, the tower over the field, the spring, and the wreath on the low branch.
stops.quote: This embroidery represents the landscape where Joan, starting at the age of 13, received visions of the archangels Michael and Gabriel, and the three virgin martyr saints: Catherine, Barbara and Margaret.
stops.quote_source: Ekaterina Sinchinova, artist's description within 'Domremy. The story of the picture,' katrinvates.com/blog/blbrj44pjcc57mrf90eunqqwektyzb
suggested_refs: The artist's own historical note on the Domremy panel, naming all three martyrs

segments.name: What the Thread Walks: the Hill Above the Meuse

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Rock the seneschal memorized
stops.date_confidence: attested for the entry into Jerusalem under the treaty of 1229; pin inherited byte-identical from joffrey_bourlemont.journey.json, which uses 31.7784, 35.2298 at three stops
stops.campa: Two centuries before the beech is old enough to be famous, a boy out of the Vosges stands at the edge of the Haram and looks a long time at the Dome above the Rock, memorizing it for children he does not yet know. Joffrey de Bourlemont will carry that image home over the sea and hand it to the children dancing under a tree in his own valley. Sinchinova's needle inherits it at one remove: the tower she works into the hillside is the tower he built when he came back, and the well is the well he sank.
suggested_refs: The Dome of the Rock, seen from the pilgrim crowd in 1229 by the future seneschal of Navarre
sources: katrinvates.com/blog, the artist naming 'the family of Joffrey Bourlemont'

stops.name: Domremy, the well and the tower at the tree's foot
stops.date_confidence: traditional, following joffrey_bourlemont.journey.json, which dates the return and the building at the tree to the mid-1240s; pin inherited byte-identical from that file and from joan_of_arc.journey.json and saint_barbara.journey.json
stops.campa: Home from the Holy Land in the year Jerusalem falls, the seneschal builds a well at the foot of the great beech and raises a watchtower over the field, and the country begins to call the spring the Fountain of the Fevered. Pierre de Bourlemont is remembered under the same boughs, meeting a lady called Fee, in a romance a godmother will tell to a child and then repeat to notaries. The same surname runs south as well, to Assisi and to Pica, mother of Francis. Every one of these objects is in the embroidery.
suggested_refs: The well and the watchtower at the Arbre des Dames, built c. 1245
sources: joffrey_bourlemont.journey.json (the spring, the well built at the tree's foot)

stops.name: Domremy-la-Pucelle, the house by the church
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the day is the Epiphany tradition and not a documented date, the year is attested through the rehabilitation depositions of 1456, and the pin is inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: In a stone house beside the church of Saint-Remy a girl is born to Jacques d'Arc and Isabelle Romee, and the parish is renamed la Pucelle for her in 1578. Joan of Arc is the name the world settles on; the hillside knows her as one of the children of Domremy and Greux. The embroidery does not show the house. It shows the hill above it, which is where the child spends the part of her life the picture is about, in a valley whose lord has died childless in the year of her birth.
suggested_refs: The Maison natale de Jeanne d'Arc, beside the church in the village core
sources: Proces en nullite de la condamnation de Jeanne d'Arc (1455-56), witness depositions

stops.name: Domremy, the church of Saint-Remy
stops.date_confidence: undated; the rehabilitation witnesses attest the habit of daily Mass and no year, so the date is a placeholder inside her childhood; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: She is baptized here and hears Mass here daily, and the neighbours will say so to the notaries thirty-six years later, under oath, in the inquiry that unmakes the sentence. The church stands a hundred paces from the tree and does not appear in the embroidery either. Sinchinova shows the field instead of the sacrament. She gives the ground where the girls dance, and that ground is what the judges of 1431 spend whole hours asking her about. The sacrament is not what anyone was on trial for.
suggested_refs: Eglise Saint-Remy de Domremy, classed monument historique by decree of 11 May 1946
sources: Rehabilitation trial testimony of Domremy neighbours, 1456

stops.name: Domremy, the Tree of Bourlemont in the fair May
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the May and Laetare Sunday gatherings are attested in the 1431 interrogation and in the 1456 depositions without a year being fixed to any one of them
stops.campa: The children come up from the village with bread and go under the beech the country calls the Ladies' Tree, They sing there, they dance, they hang garlands of flower and leaf on the branches. Sinchinova hangs one herself: in the finished picture a single wreath rests on a low bough of the beech. The trial of 1431 spent whole sessions questioning her about those garlands, and the artist has read the trial before she threads the needle. Her own note calls the tree a thousand years old and the forest home to dragons.
stops.quote: Testimony reveals the children of Domrémy would sing and dance around the giant beechwood 'fairy tree', and leave flower garlands on its branches, as gifts for the fairies.
suggested_refs: L'Arbre des Fees, the Ladies' Tree of the Bourlemont fief above Domremy
sources: Proces de condamnation, 1431, interrogation on the arbre des fees

stops.name: Domremy, the spring the fevered drink
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the trial attests that she drank from the spring, the curative reputation is local folklore recorded later, and the pin is inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json (la Fontaine des Fievreux)
stops.campa: Beside the tree the spring runs, and the sick come to drink against fever. At her trial she will admit drinking from it and deny ever having seen a fairy there, which is the exact shape of everything she says under interrogation: the fact conceded, the enchantment refused. The embroidery puts the wellhead in the middle distance, stone and water, with no fairy in it. She stitched only what the sworn record allows. Everything the interrogation refused to grant her is missing from the linen too.
suggested_refs: La Fontaine des Fievreux, the spring at the tree's foot

stops.name: Domremy, the Bois Chenu the picture leaves out
stops.date_confidence: traditional and commemorative, not attested; her own testimony places the first vision c. 1425 in her father's garden with the voice coming from the direction of the church, and the Bois Chenu is the site the nineteenth-century basilica marks, tied to the prophecy of a maid coming out of that wood
stops.campa: Above the village the oak wood carries an old prophecy about a maid who will come out of the Bois Chenu, and a basilica will be raised here in the nineteenth century to mark the place where she is said to have heard her voices. She did not say it happened here. She said the first voice came in her father's garden, from the direction of the church, when she was thirteen. The embroidery leaves the wood as a dark mass at the edge, which is roughly the standing the record gives it.
suggested_refs: The Basilique du Bois-Chenu, built to mark the traditional site of the voices
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Joan of Arc' (first vision in her father's garden, c. 1425)

stops.name: Greux, the chapel of Notre-Dame de Bermont
stops.date_confidence: undated; the rehabilitation witnesses attest the Saturday pilgrimage habit and give no year, and the coordinate is this report's own approximation north of Greux, with no atlas precedent and no pool value behind it
stops.campa: North of the village, up past Greux, a twelfth-century chapel stands where she walks almost every Saturday to leave candles, and the neighbours remember the habit clearly enough to swear to it in 1456. Mark Twain will follow this road in a novel and give the walk to a narrator born at Neufchateau. The chapel is not in the embroidery. Sinchinova's picture holds one hillside and leaves out the rest of the parish, the chapel and the road to it among the things it does not contain.
suggested_refs: Chapelle Notre-Dame de Bermont, listed monument historique 1998
sources: Rehabilitation trial testimony, 1456, deposition of Mengette and other Domremy witnesses

stops.name: Domremy, the tower and the third sister
stops.date_confidence: the date and the pin are both inherited byte-identical from catherine_alexandria.journey.json, which fixes its Ladies' Tree stop at 1428-03-14 and 48.43, 5.671; note that the corpus carries two pins for one tree and the disagreement is preserved rather than smoothed; this stop closes the segment so that the segment's years run forward
stops.campa: The parchment keeps Catherine and Margaret at her side and drops the third. Barbara is the one who carries a tower, and there is a tower standing over this field with a single window in it, and Sinchinova puts them in one picture. She names all three herself, on her own site: Catherine, Barbara and Margaret, the same triad the Fourteen Holy Helpers rhyme on a Rhineland altar. Two other accounts of those saints cite her by name for this same interpolation, both dating the work to January 2023.
suggested_refs: Katrin Vates (Ekaterina Sinchinova), 'Domremy' embroidery, January 2023, the tree, the well, and the tower

segments.name: The Roads the Picture Does Not Take

stops.name: Vaucouleurs, the Porte de France
stops.date_confidence: traditional for the day of departure; the two audiences with Robert de Baudricourt in May 1428 and January 1429 are attested in the condemnation record and in the depositions of Bertrand de Poulengy and Jean de Metz; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: Twice she comes to the garrison commander here, turned away in May and given an escort in January, and she rides out through the town gate that still stands and that will be renamed for her. This is the first place the hillside cannot follow her to. From the tree it is a day's ride north. The girl who hung garlands goes out of the parish here and never comes back into it alive, and no later stop in her life stands closer to the beech than this one. The embroidery stops at the parish boundary and stays there.
suggested_refs: The Porte de France at Vaucouleurs, still standing
sources: Proces de condamnation and rehabilitation testimony of Poulengy and Jean de Metz

stops.name: Chinon, the hall
stops.date_confidence: the arrival at Chinon is attested to 6 March 1429 and the audience with Charles VII two days later; an earlier research pass conflated the two and invented a 'Sainte-Catherine hall' at Chinon, which does not exist, the Catherine association belonging to Fierbois
stops.campa: She arrives at the castle on the sixth of March and Charles receives her two days later, lodged in the meantime in the Tour du Coudray. The chronicle says she picked him out of a crowd of courtiers who had dressed a decoy; the trial record, which is the document she herself is on oath in, does not describe the scene in that form. Both versions stand here, with neither preferred over the other. Nothing of this is in the embroidery, which shows a well and a tree and a tower and a wreath on a low branch.
suggested_refs: The Logis Royal and the Tour du Coudray, Chateau de Chinon

stops.name: Sainte-Catherine-de-Fierbois, the sword behind the altar
stops.date_confidence: attested in her own condemnation testimony as to the sword and the five crosses; the month is the campaign window and not a documented day; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: She sends word that a sword lies buried behind the altar of this church, marked with five crosses, and it is found there, and she says she has never been inside the building. The church is Catherine's, one of the two names the parchment keeps and one of the three the embroidery restores. The steel comes up out of the ground at a saint's altar, and the whole line, tree to sword, reads as one thread: what is buried at the root comes up as a weapon.
suggested_refs: The sword of Fierbois, found behind the altar marked with five crosses
sources: Proces de condamnation, 1431, testimony on the sword of Fierbois

stops.name: Orleans, the siege lifted
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the Journal du siege d'Orleans; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: The English pull back from the city on the eighth of May, and it gives her the name she is known by afterwards. She was wounded above the breast at the bridge fort the day before, withdrew, and went back into the fighting. From the hillside above the Meuse this is eight weeks away and unimaginable. Sinchinova sets her picture in the years before any of this happens. She stitched a childhood and not a campaign, and everything else recorded here about Joan of Arc hangs on that one panel of a hill.
suggested_refs: The Cathedrale Sainte-Croix d'Orleans, where the city gave thanks on 8 May 1429

stops.name: Reims, the anointing
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: Charles is anointed and crowned in the cathedral with her standing at the altar holding her banner, and she says afterwards that it had borne the burden and had earned the honour. Lionel Royer will paint this scene four and a half centuries later, and his canvas becomes the image France teaches. Two ways of making the same girl visible: oil at national scale, and floss on linen at twenty inches by thirty, showing the field she left rather than the church she reached.
suggested_refs: Lionel Royer, 'Jeanne d'Arc au sacre de Charles VII', 1880s
sources: Proces de condamnation, 1431, her testimony on the coronation and her banner

stops.name: Paris, the assault on the Porte Saint-Honore
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json, which uses 48.8632, 2.3336 here and 48.9356, 2.36 for Saint-Denis, and not the 48.8566, 2.3522 an earlier research pass reported as canonical
stops.campa: A crossbow bolt goes through her thigh at the ditch before the gate, and the king orders the withdrawal the next day. Afterwards she lays her armour before the shrine at Saint-Denis, a soldier's votive and not a farewell. Luc-Olivier Merson will paint her too, in the register of the century that made her a national image. The embroidery declines all of it. There is no armour in it, no banner, no wound, no king. Everything the century painted, she leaves out.
suggested_refs: The Basilica of Saint-Denis, where the armour was laid, at 48.9356, 2.36 in the atlas

stops.name: Rouen, the Vieux-Marche
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the scattering of the ashes in the Seine is well-attested tradition rather than trial record; pin inherited byte-identical from joan_of_arc.journey.json
stops.campa: She is burned in the market square, and the ashes are thrown into the Seine so that there will be nothing left to keep. Fifteen interrogation sessions ran between February and March, then the ordinary trial from the twenty-sixth of March, and a monk named Jean Tressart is recorded saying afterwards that they had burned a saint. There is no grave. Any monument to her has to be made rather than visited, and five and a half centuries later a woman in Maryland makes one out of linen and floss.
suggested_refs: The Place du Vieux-Marche at Rouen, and the absence of any grave
sources: Proces de condamnation, 1431, and eyewitness chronicle accounts
en.wikipedia, 'Trial of Joan of Arc' (fifteen interrogation sessions, 21 February to 17 March 1431)

stops.name: Rouen, the sentence annulled
stops.date_confidence: the date is attested and the venue is not; the retrial opened at Notre-Dame de Rouen on 7 November 1455, and no source consulted places the July 1456 verdict in the cathedral, so the atlas says only that it was delivered at Rouen and pins the archiepiscopal quarter approximately
stops.campa: Twenty-five years later the court declares her innocent and annuls the condemnation of 1431, the Archbishop of Reims reading the verdict out. Where in the city it was read no source consulted confirms, so only Rouen itself is stated with certainty. The depositions taken for this inquiry, at Domremy, from neighbours and from a godmother, are the reason anybody can describe a tree, a spring, a garland, and a girl dancing. Without them there is no picture to stitch.
suggested_refs: Proces en nullite de la condamnation de Jeanne d'Arc, verdict of 7 July 1456
sources: Proces en nullite de la condamnation de Jeanne d'Arc, 1456

stops.name: Alexandria, Virginia, the sixtieth Woodlawn exhibition
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on katrinvates.com/art-cv, which gives no month or day for any award; the coordinate is this report's own approximation for Woodlawn, with no atlas precedent
stops.campa: At the sixtieth annual needlework exhibition she takes Second Place, Third Place, and the People's Choice Award, all three in Surface Embroidery, in the year the Domremy panel is finished. The People's Choice is the one that matters for what follows: the room voted, and the room is a room of needleworkers who can see exactly what has been done to the linen. Her CV records the year and no month. It will record this same exhibition four years running.
suggested_refs: The Woodlawn Needlework Exhibition, held at Woodlawn and the Pope-Leighey House, Alexandria

stops.name: Bethesda, the notice in the county magazine
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month via search summary only; the Bethesda Magazine article returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and the quoted sentence has not been verified against the page itself
stops.campa: A local magazine describes one of her landscapes in April, the first substantially independent description of her work that this research could locate anywhere, and the page returns a forbidden response to every attempt to read it directly. What survives is a sentence about fog and a hill in autumn, reaching this account at second hand. Everything else written about her, anywhere, is written by her. The record of a living artist can look like this, and this one does.
stops.quote: A landscape piece by Rockville artist Ekaterina Sinchinova. Fog creeps through trees glowing with colors of crimson, pine and gold on a hill in the midst of autumn.
stops.quote_source: Bethesda Magazine, April 2023, via search summary; the article itself returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch

stops.name: Alexandria, the sixty-first and the first place
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV, no month or day given
stops.campa: First Place in Surface Embroidery at Woodlawn, one rank up from the year before. The exhibition has run since the early nineteen-sixties in a house George Washington gave to his adopted daughter, and it is the oldest continuous needlework competition in the country. She has been embroidering for five years. Nineteen years she set colour that other people had chosen. Now the top prize in surface embroidery is hers, awarded in the room where the craft judges its own.
suggested_refs: The 61st Annual Woodlawn Needlework Exhibition, 2024

stops.name: North Bethesda, Strathmore and the Prism jury
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV, no month or day; the place is corrected here from the research pool, which gave 'Strathmore, Bethesda/North Bethesda' and a garbled address, Strathmore being at 10701 Rockville Pike in North Bethesda, a distinct CDP
stops.campa: Second Prize at the thirty-second annual juried exhibition, under the title Prism: Connections in Color. The venue is a nineteenth-century mansion on Rockville Pike in North Bethesda, ten minutes from her own town, and it is the building that will give her a solo show within two years. The jurors here are not needleworkers, and nothing obliges them to be impressed by the stitching. A guild award is given by people who know what the technique costs; this one is given by people who see only the picture.
suggested_refs: 'Prism: Connections in Color', Strathmore's 32nd Annual Juried Exhibition, 2024

stops.name: Germantown and Rockville, the lecture and the workshop
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV for all three engagements, no months or days given; the pin is Germantown, and the Potomac Fiber Art Guild lecture and the Rockville workshop are folded into this stop
stops.campa: She gives a lecture called Realistic Effect in Free Embroidery Style to the Art League of Germantown, and again to the Potomac Fiber Art Guild, and leads a workshop for the guild in Rockville. The title states the whole method flatly: the realistic effect, in free style, which means without a pattern and without a frame. Five years after picking up a needle with no teacher at all, she is the one standing in front of a guild explaining how the stitch is made. The guild pays her for it.
suggested_refs: 'Realistic Effect in Free Embroidery Style', her standing lecture from 2024

stops.name: Harrisonburg, Virginia, Continuing Tradition
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year on the CV, no month or day; the coordinate is this report's own approximation for the Virginia Quilt Museum
stops.campa: Her work enters Continuing Tradition: Contemporary Embroidery at the Virginia Quilt Museum, the first institutional setting on her CV that is not a competition. A prize says the work is good. A group show under that title says the work belongs to a lineage, and the lineage is the one the Domremy panel reached into when it hung a garland on a fifteenth-century branch. The CV gives the show a year and no dates at all, and no catalogue of it was located anywhere.
suggested_refs: 'Continuing Tradition: Contemporary Embroidery', Virginia Quilt Museum, 2025

stops.name: Alexandria, the sixty-second and the sixty-third
stops.date_confidence: two years folded into one stop, 2025 and 2026, both attested to the year on the CV and neither to a month or a day
stops.campa: First Place and Second Place at the sixty-second Woodlawn, and at the sixty-third the Judge's Choice Award, First Place, and a separate Second Place again. Four consecutive years, ten awards, one category. It is the only hard shape in the whole career record: everything else is a magazine credit or a self-published date, and this is a jury of the craft returning the same verdict four times running in the same room in Virginia. The CV gives the years and never a day.
suggested_refs: The 62nd and 63rd Annual Woodlawn Needlework Exhibitions, 2025 and 2026

stops.campa: Her first solo exhibition opens in the Invitational Gallery of the mansion, under the title The Placid Surface, billed as a local artist's first show in that room and running on into the new year. The opening date cannot be confirmed: the venue's own page refuses to be read, and the announcement reaching the record comes through a summary. What is certain is the CV line, which spans two years, and the title, which is a needleworker's joke about what a flat piece of linen conceals.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the same thread in another hemisphere
stops.date_confidence: not an event date at all; this stop records a standing adjacency rather than a meeting, so it is placed at the time of the research alongside the other present-day stops, and no document connects any of these artists to Sinchinova, the grouping being the corpus's own in QUEUE.md; the pin is inherited byte-identical from leo_chiachio.journey.json
stops.campa: The coordinate sits in the queue's embroidery-and-textile block, adjacency and nothing more. No document ties Sinchinova to Argentina, to any Argentine collaborator, or to any other artist working in thread anywhere outside her own Rockville practice. What her own record shows instead is a publication circuit that already spans five continents without a single named collaborator: Colossal in Chicago, Le Temps De Broder in Switzerland, frankie in Melbourne, DPI in Taipei, Stitch&Trip in Seoul, eleven outlets across nine countries by the end of 2022, every one of them a magazine or a website reprinting a photograph, not a studio she shares.
suggested_refs: The embroidery cluster in QUEUE.md, lines 259-261 and 301, an adjacency rather than a documented relation

stops.name: Rockville, no tomb
stops.date_confidence: the date of this research, not an event; she is living and working, and the brief's standard closing question of a tomb and its fate does not apply to her
stops.campa: The journey ends where it cannot close. She is alive, working, posting, teaching, selling kits, and there is no grave, no plaque, no monument, and no catalogue to reach the end of. No edition or reproduction of the Domremy panel was located anywhere; it appears to be a single object in private hands, and where it now hangs no source says. She stitched a hillside that holds no grave, and she has no grave herself. Both are recorded here as gaps and not as endings.
suggested_refs: The Domremy panel, present whereabouts unrecorded, the open question this journey leaves
